To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the induction of contact allergy is dependent on Langerhans cell (LC) function only in some strains (or individuals) of mice, and that this LC-dependent phenotype is genetically determined by at least three, and possibly four, independent genetic factors, one of which is H-2.

the induction of contact sensitization is dependent on normal LC numbers at the site of hapten painting in some strains of inbred mice, whereas in others, alternative mechanisms allow for the development of contact hypersensitivity even when LC are depleted by low-dose UV radiation.

1) UVB radiation produces profound depletion of epimermal Langerhens cells at UVB-irradiated sites, but 2) the capacity of a skin surface to support the development of CH after UVB radiation is dependent on genetic factors, and 3) at least three, and probably four, genetic loci participate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis for the effects of UV light on the immune response.
the elucidation of the genetic basis for UVB-related immunomodulation of the contact sensitivity response in mice.
the genetic basis of the capacity of UVB radiation to alter the capacity of the epidermis to support the induction and elicitation of CH.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genetic basis of the UVB effect on CH induction is complex.
there are at least two genetic loci that are involved in determining susceptibility and resistance to UVB effects on the induction of CH in mice.
UVB radiation has profound effects on the epidermis and that the genetic control of the induction of contact sensitization is more complex than previously believed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
UVB radiation induces a state of cutaneous unresponsiveness to contact hypersensitivity in some strains of genetically defined mice.
the induction of contact sensitivity in mice requires the presence of Langerhans cell at the site of hapten application.
the genetic basis of the induction of CH is more complex than previously thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
UVB radiation can have different effects on the induction of CH in different strains of mice, and that the capacity to induce CH is not necessarily dependent on normal numbers and function of LC.
UVB radiation has a profound impact on cutaneous immunity, but that this effect is genetically determined and not universal.
UVB-induced immunosuppression is a genetically complex phenomenon.
